items.title: Equity mutual funds inflow surges 31% to ₹38,306 crore in September

Equity mutual fund schemes attracted a net inflow of Rs 38,306 crore in September, rising 31 per cent from the preceding month, driven by strong investor interest in mid-cap and small-cap funds despite underperformance in the equity market.
The inflow was higher than Rs 29,329 crore recorded in August, according to data released by the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) on Monday.
Among equity categories, small-cap funds attracted the highest net inflow of Rs 9,039 crore, followed by mid-cap funds at Rs 7,835 crore. Large-cap funds, meanwhile, saw net inflows of Rs 860 crore during the month.
" Equity inflows jumped sharply in a month when markets were under pressure. Much of that reflects the lasting faith Indian investors have in equities as one of the best long-term routes to wealth creation. items.title: Fusion CX fixes IPO price band at ₹275-289 per share, issue size at ₹702 cr
items.summary:
AI-powered customer experience solutions provider Fusion CX Ltd on Friday fixed the price band of Rs 275-289 per share for its Rs 702 crore Initial Public Offering (IPO), which will open for subscription on October 14.
At the upper end of the price band, Fusion CX is expected to command a post-issue market capitalisation of over Rs 4,170 crore.
The three-day public issue will close on October 16, while bidding by anchor investors is scheduled for October 13, according to a public announcement.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 500 crore and an Offer For Sale (OFS) of shares aggregating up to Rs 202 crore by existing shareholders, P N S Business Pvt Ltd and Rasish Consultants Pvt Ltd.
The company had initially planned to raise up to Rs 1,000 crore through its IPO, according to its draft red herring prospectus filed with Sebi in May 2025. However, the proposed issue size has since been reduced to Rs 702 crore.

items.title: WazirX futures trading volume jumps 236% in Q3 as exchange expands AI tools
items.summary:
Indian cryptocurrency exchange WazirX said its futures trading volume rose 236 per cent  between the beginning of July and the end of September, as it expanded derivatives offerings, introduced AI-powered trading tools and stepped up tax-reporting and compliance features.
Trading volume at its September peak was about 345 per cent above early-July levels, while the number of daily futures traders was approximately 279 per cent higher toward the end of the quarter, the company said in a statement on Friday.
The exchange's July-September expansion included the launch of USDT-denominated perpetual futures with Indian rupee margin, an AI trading assistant, automated margin top-ups and a free cryptocurrency tax-reporting platform. The developments reflect a push to broaden access to derivatives trading while giving users more tools to manage positions and track transactions.'
